record_identity.title: Waymo robotaxis contributed to San Francisco gridlock during major power outage

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Waymo robotaxis contributed to San Francisco gridlock during major power outage
incident_identity.date_basis: Waymo identifies 20 December 2025 as the date of the San Francisco outage and fleet response.

summary: On 20 December 2025, a major San Francisco power outage disabled traffic signals. Waymo reported crossing more than 7,000 dark signals, but simultaneous remote-confirmation requests created a backlog. Delayed vehicles contributed to congestion alongside the wider outage. Later city reporting described a Waymo obstructing the substation fire response, a disabled vehicle delaying an ambulance by 40 minutes, and another blocking a fire-response unit. Dispatchers encountered long waits on the Waymo hotline. Seven reported obstructions affected Muni vehicles, including one delayed by 41 minutes. Waymo paused service and directed staged fleet retrieval. Reports continued after the pause. On 23 December it announced fleet-wide outage-context updates and planned emergency-protocol, city-coordination and responder-training improvements. The city later sought stronger resilience planning and access to stoppage data.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Waymo reports a correlated confirmation-request backlog and a contribution to congestion, rather than sole responsibility for citywide gridlock. Its December 23 account describes a pause and staged retrieval, and states that technical updates were rolling out while operational improvements were planned. SFMTA’s February 13 filing on behalf of city response agencies reports three distinct impacts on fire and ambulance operations, prolonged hotline holds and seven transit obstructions. One ambulance arrival was delayed by 40 minutes and one Muni vehicle by 41 minutes. The city identified 42 unduplicated AV reports from 2 p.m. to midnight. Its account of Waymo-disclosed figures identifies 829 vehicles and 1,593 stoppages exceeding two minutes, with 96% resolved without manual retrieval. These denominators differ: reported locations, vehicles and stoppage events must not be equated. The filing challenges an inference that service suspension immediately cleared every obstruction. It does not establish collision, injury, every delay’s internal mechanism or sole fleet causation of wider outage effects.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence exposed correlated remote-assistance demand and a separately evidenced emergency-signal delivery problem. City reports connect stalled hotline requests to unresolved vehicle obstructions. Service suspension and staged retrieval are supported responses, but they did not immediately clear every obstruction. The reported emergency and transit delays strengthen the material operational-harm basis. The evidence does not assign the whole city outage to Waymo or establish collision or injury.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case shows that autonomy systems must be tested for correlated edge cases in which many units simultaneously seek remote confirmation during degraded public infrastructure.
assessment_boundaries: The external power failure and vehicle contribution are distinct. City operational records are not a comprehensive causal account of gridlock.
No reviewed source establishes collision or injury attributable to this occurrence. Emergency and transit obstruction are reported by city agencies.
The vehicle confirmation queue and the first-responder hotline are separate response channels. Their exact internal relationship is not established.
The technical rollout and proposed operational improvements lack independently inspected completion and effectiveness evidence.

clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: This timed emergency-service effect differs from citywide congestion and from the other fire responses.

clauses.source_paraphrase: A fire-response unit was blocked near Grant Avenue. Avoid-area messages were sent at 5:32 and 5:37 p.m.; a dispatcher seeking removal at 5:43 remained on hold at 5:53.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Produced protective requests require timely delivery to a capable response point.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: City dispatchers produced requests to move vehicles obstructing emergency response. The first-responder hotline stalled those requests on prolonged holds while obstructions persisted. A 40-minute ambulance delay and repeat relocation requests establish a material failure to deliver the signal in time for its required response. The internal queue or staffing fault remains unknown.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Across overlapping emergency responses, dispatchers made 31 hotline calls totalling two hours and 36 minutes, mostly on hold. The Mayor contacted Waymo directly.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Aggregate calls contextualise the preceding responses; they are not 31 additional independently reconstructed obstructions.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The city reports prolonged holds on the designated response channel, with a separate mayoral escalation. Requests did not reliably reach timely disposition while the emergency obstructions required intervention.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Seven reported immobilised Waymo obstructions affected Muni vehicles; one vehicle was delayed by 41 minutes.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Transit disruption is separate from fire, ambulance and hotline effects.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Waymo paused service and directed vehicles to park and return to depots in waves. City reports continued after the reported 5:55 p.m. suspension.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Stopping new service and clearing existing obstructions are distinct protective effects.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The pause and retrieval were intended to reduce congestion and emergency obstruction. Later reports show remaining obstructions, but do not resolve the required clearance interval or each vehicle’s control and retrieval state. A bounded adequate-control outcome is therefore not established.

clauses.adjudication_note: The pause is established. Required clearing performance and the control state of each continuing obstruction remain unresolved.

clauses.source_paraphrase: On December 23, Waymo said outage-context updates were rolling out and that it would improve protocols, city coordination and responder training.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: An announced rollout or plan is distinct from verified implementation and effectiveness.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The February city filing sought resilience planning, agency consultation, exercises and access to stoppage data; it cited 1,593 provider-reported stoppages among 829 vehicles.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Later review and aggregate disclosure are distinct from the December operational responses. The city’s estimates and requests are not regulatory findings.
